meta.title: Climbing the AI Bubble Wall of Worry
meta.thread_line: 7 threads · the real bubble · breadth signals · agent compute demand · concentrated alpha · bank apocalypse via Stripe · tokenization and privacy · labor vs capital

snapshot: Weekly speed-round answering Ray Dalio's "AI bubble may burst": the bubble is in **rate-dependent zombie companies**, not the digital economy; position long AI, short the rest.
No unwind in the data: the market shrugged off a pandemic, the fastest hikes since the 1980s, the largest bank run, tariffs and $200-oil fears; **20-30% corrections yes, bubble bursts no**.
Demand still beats supply because the new buyer is **agents, not humans**: thousands now, billions next year, and they "eat tokens" faster than efficiency can offset.
Alpha is extremely concentrated: 71% of his 59 agentic names in the S&P 1500 beat the index since ChatGPT vs 24% of the universe; next leg is **components and crypto**.
"Bank apocalypse" clarified: not a short call, a SaaS-style multiple compression within ~9 months, with **Stripe** as the case study (41% revenue growth, agent wallets, OpenRouter deal).
Tokenization is the underpriced risk: 24/7 trading hurts market-neutral funds, options desks and levered multistrats; he wants to be **long privacy** (Zcash, Near).
Labor is the soft spot: healthcare hiring slowing, nobody hiring, profits up while labor isn't; **2027 = compute, AI acceleration and crypto year**.
Captions end on the sign-off ("see you next"); no content lost.

themes.title: The bubble is in zombies that need zero rates, not in AI
themes.lead: Higher rates are exposing old-economy companies that survived on cheap debt; that is the bubble, and it is unwinding without dragging the AI economy down.
bullets: Ray Dalio said the AI bubble "may burst" on rising rates; Visser counts many Dalio bubble calls since 2012 and calls it an **endgame bias** shared by perma-bears who are "selling something".

Three bubble types: speculative (dot-com Cisco at 100 P/E vs Nvidia at ~15), capacity (supply ahead of demand) and credit (housing); none shows up, and much AI debt is **asset-backed against compute**.
His AI risk scorecard (an LLM fed his weekly data, scoring on its own): demand strong, compute still scarce, **capital on watch list** as funding needs push yields up, valuation fine on PEG.

"400 stocks go down and 100 go higher" because zombies kept alive by low rates are losing; a Jason Furman chart is "long AI short the rest of the world"; borrowers have termed out debt and liquidity is ample.

Credit: CCCs weakening vs high yield but BBBs are not ("getting rid of the weak"); the Morgan Stanley leverage factor is falling with the S&P at highs; he worries only when **hyperscalers** fall with it. Johnson Redbook consumer spending still fine.

Drawdowns since the iPhone recover fast: ~40% (COVID), ~30% (2022), 20% (tariffs). Longest gaps without a new high since Dec 1969: 1973 (7 years), 2000 (back ~2007), 2007 (back 2013), 2022 (only **500 days**, fourth longest). A pandemic, the fastest hikes since the 1980s, the largest bank run, tariffs and $200-oil/Strait of Hormuz fears all failed to break it.

Origin story: stopped traveling to China in 2012-13, went to Silicon Valley to understand why Amazon could trade at "infinity P/E"; says barely 2% of people over 50 use AI, so the money-holders fear bubbles.

quote.text: At some point, you have to admit there's no bubble burst.

themes.status: EQUAL-WEIGHT MACD BUY FIRED THIS WEEK
themes.title: Bad breadth is a buy signal in the digital economy
themes.lead: Weak breadth just means rate-sensitive zombies are oversold; when it washes out, equal-weight bounces, and this week's signal has a perfect record since 2007.
bullets: Share above the 200-day: utilities **18%**, staples 33%, household durables 30%, autos 12% vs technology 73%, financials 74%; all the weak ones are rate-sensitive.
Equal-weight S&P (SPW) got an oversold **MACD buy signal** this week; since 2007 it was higher 6 months later 22 of 22 times (100%), 91% at 3 months, 90% at 12 months.
Breadth is "like a high VIX": on the day **OpenAI** headlines caused panic, equal weight rose as hedge funds covered shorts on the old economy.
S&P is up 14% this year and only **energy and tech** beat it; the RSI on breadth hit rare oversold levels last week.
Europe vs US since the iPhone (July 1, 2007) is the AI trade in reverse; the US is **56%** technology; IWM vs QQQ is the same trade, so "broadening out" works only in brief bursts.

10-year yield shows a **triple RSI divergence** against new price highs, looking "tired"; the MOVE index (bond vol) had an outside reversal week; even flat yields a year out are no reason to be bearish stocks.
The Economist's "Will bonds blow up?" cover lands the same week as Dalio; he reads both as contrarian reversal signs for bonds and rate-sensitive assets.

themes.title: Agents, not humans, are the demand side, so compute stays short
themes.lead: Every past bubble had humans on both sides; agents multiply far faster than nominal GDP and need tokens, so supply cannot catch up.
bullets: Agents: "thousands" now, **billions next year**, then trillions, each working ~5x human hours; efficiency gains as the answer are "hocus pocus".
Compute is the new oil: oil grows with nominal GDP because humans set demand; agents are not nominal GDP, they grow "faster than rabbits and cockroaches".
His run-rate model: **$70B** annualized OpenAI revenue by year-end and ~$100B for Anthropic; OpenAI has since logged "hundreds more math results" that got no press.
Aaron Levie: compute for personal agents, agent swarms and 24/7 background agents "is going to be insane", said in response to the hardware Meta's Muse needs for 100M users (of its 3B).
Instinct AI's founder: compute needs "orders of magnitude more" than thought; **Cloudflare** forecast (March 2026) AI bots overtake web traffic by 2027, then said it already happened.
**Lumentum**'s CEO says it is sold out through 2029. A widely shared revenue-math paper: "The math is right. The future is completely wrong"; it was written before personal agents existed.

Exponential frame: Kurzweil's curve put one human brain ~2021 and all human brains (ASI) by 2050; Karpathy said on Dwarkesh agents were a decade away, a year before they arrived. Next year's innovation "equivalent to like a decade"; the S&P is an innovation index.
Don't trade the **personal-agent race** (Meta's Muse, Amazon's Alexa, Apple's Siri, Google): same TAM, extreme competition, unclear profits (discussed with Pomp); trade the compute instead.

themes.status: LONG AGENTIC AI, SHORT THE REST
themes.title: Alpha lives in a narrow agentic basket; diversification loses
themes.lead: Since ChatGPT, almost every source of outperformance has been the physical AI build, so a stock picker has to concentrate.
bullets: Phase 1 was **Nvidia** plus power (Vistra, turbines); Opus 4.5 in November started phase 2, memory: Micron went 100 to 200 in seven months, then doubled again in five; "everyone missed the memory trade".
Next: two smaller component areas he expects to deliver **three and four baggers**; detail goes to subscribers.
Of his agentic basket, 59 names sit in the S&P 1500 and **71%** have beaten it since ChatGPT (Nov 2022) vs 24% of the universe; winner-vs-loser median spreads are massive.
2021-26 winners: semis, tech hardware, energy, capital goods; media/entertainment (Netflix, Google) only market-perform; **software** fell out of the 10-year winners list after leading two years ago.
Tech destroyed incumbents: Apple vs Garmin and camera makers, Amazon vs malls, Google vs newspapers and ads, Netflix; still around, not investable.
Market-structure buckets for funds: **winner** (semis), adapter, or disrupted (SaaS); middle names "eventually get thrown" into one; banks sit there now.
His agentic portfolio is in a cup-and-handle; breakout "probably after the midterms"; S&P made another all-time high this week.

quote.text: Everyone missed the memory trade. everyone will miss these two.

themes.status: MULTIPLE COMPRESSION, NOT A SHORT CALL
themes.title: Bank apocalypse: Stripe is building the bank agents will use
themes.lead: Banks face a SaaS-style derating within ~9 months as consumer agents arrive, and Stripe's growth shows who takes the fast-growing customers.
bullets: Bloomberg wrote up his "bank apocalypse" video without asking him; clarification: banks won't collapse and he isn't shorting them, but a revenue "flinch" in the **next nine months** triggers SaaS-style repricing as consumer agents (Siri etc.) land next year.
Stripe built agent rails: 288 launches, agent wallets powered by Link, acquired **Privy** (wallets), Metronome (metered billing), Bridge (stablecoins) and now OpenRouter (token routing).

Stripe letter: "January 1st marked the beginning of the singularity"; internet economic infrastructure is mostly the same thing as AI's. His Substack "Stripe Sessions and the coming agentic commerce economy" (June 30, 2026).
H1: net revenue +41%, billing +71%, free cash flow +43%; Capital over **100,000** active loans; Connect platforms activating at 2x last year's rate; Treasury among fastest-growing products ever.
Citigroup 226,000 employees vs Stripe 10,000: $214B vs $160B valuations, ~**15x** per employee; Google 199,000 vs Anthropic 6,100, also ~15x.
SWIFT is too old and too hackable: bank to Robinhood took 5 days, Robinhood to Coinbase 5 seconds; agents need same-second settlement and metered micro-billing.

Bears' inconsistency: tokens get cheaper, yet agents will only pay through **Mastercard and Visa**. Thousands of businesses launch on Stripe every few hours; a ladder of AI apps ($2K, $10K, ten at $12K) lets people quit jobs and erodes slow incumbents ("Think Ford verse Tesla and humanoids").

themes.title: Tokenization will break 9-to-4 risk models; privacy is the crypto theme
themes.lead: Crypto is where he sees the big money, because funds won't own it until they have to, and agents make privacy a control problem.
bullets: Crypto upside needs fundamentals plus **fund flows** crossing over; hedge and mutual funds "are not going to buy the crypto side until they have to".

Moving from 32.5 hours of equity trading to **168 hours** reprices options and liquidity; "horrible" for market-neutral funds, options traders and levered multistrats (cites LTCM and Axie Infinity on risk repricing).
Vitalik Buterin at OKX Singapore: agentic AI turns privacy into "a control problem not just a policy problem"; Visser wants to be **long privacy** (Zcash, Near).

Adoption headlines: IMF says tokenized assets grew rapidly; OKX filed with the SEC for tokenized stock trading; Samsung added USDC to Samsung Wallet; **Standard Chartered** launched Singapore crypto custody.
Citrini Research's "Breaking the Wall" (DeFi vs banks) recommended; new report: the 46-token index as "crypto guardrails for the agentic economy", plus a multi-agent prompt for Claude Code or Codex.

themes.title: Strong investment cycle, weakening labor market
themes.lead: Earnings can outrun higher rates, but jobs are already rolling over, and he expects that to pressure bonds and wages next year.
bullets: Henry McVey (KKR, ex-Morgan Stanley): the global investment cycle is "broader, more durable, and probably more inflationary"; Europe stronger than expected, Asia strong, defense and infrastructure booming.
McVey: earnings strong enough to overcome higher rates; judge **nominal GDP vs EPS** vs rates, not rates alone. The conundrum: corporate profits rising rapidly while labor isn't.
Warren Pies: job losses are already here. Healthcare openings and jobs slowed over the last six months; without healthcare, **negative payroll prints** become regular.
Jobs plentiful vs hard to get is weakening; claims won't rise but "nobody's hiring", bad for wages; he expects jobs to pressure the bond market soon.
Agency advice: build an AI stack and side businesses, give kids the tools, and avoid big organizations that will "cap pay and use agents".
themes.watch: The agency advice doubles as a pitch for his subscription tiers.

takeaways.title: Treat oversold equal-weight breadth as a buy signal, not a top warning, while tech breadth stays above 70%.
Express the agent thesis through compute and components, not by picking the personal-agent winner.
Re-underwrite bank holdings against Stripe-style rails before consumer agents hit revenue next year.
Study privacy chains (Zcash, Near) and tokenization before institutions are forced in.
Stress-test options and levered market-neutral books for 168-hour tokenized trading.
Build income streams on your own AI stack instead of relying on a large employer's payroll.
